finding.claim: The /fetch2 endpoint fetches a user-supplied URL. The only check is that the scheme is http or https, so an attacker can reach loopback, RFC-1918 and cloud metadata addresses (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/). Redirects are followed, so an external URL can also redirect to an internal one. The response body (first 200 chars) is returned to the caller, so this is full-read SSRF. Severity HIGH.
finding.source: request.args.get("url") at views.py:19 (query parameter 'url', unauthenticated Flask route)
finding.sink: requests.get(url, timeout=5) at views.py:22 (allow_redirects defaults to True)

trace.note: is_http_url(url) is called. It returns urlparse(url).scheme in ("http","https") (validators.py:6-7), a scheme-only check that does not restrict host or IP.
requests.get(url, timeout=5) is called with redirects followed, and .text[:200] is returned in the JSON response

finding.guards_checked: is_http_url is scheme-only and does not close SSRF. There is no hostname allowlist, no IP resolution or blocklist, and redirects are not disabled or re-validated. There is no authentication decorator on the route. Redirect following is on by default, which also defeats any 'external only' assumption.

verdict.guard_found: none (only is_http_url scheme check at validators.py:6-7; no auth decorator, no host/IP check, redirects not disabled)
verdict.reason: views.py:19-22 passes the unauthenticated query param `url` through the scheme-only is_http_url (validators.py:7) to requests.get with default redirect following, and returns the body's first 200 chars, with no host or IP guard (unlike /fetch at views.py:12-14, which uses is_safe_url and allow_redirects=False).

finding.claim: The /fetch endpoint is guarded by is_safe_url, which is a DNS-resolution blocklist and not a strict hostname allowlist. It resolves the hostname once in validators.py to check the IPs, then requests.get resolves it again independently. An attacker-controlled DNS server can answer with a public IP for the check and 127.0.0.1 or 169.254.169.254 for the fetch (DNS rebinding / TOCTOU). The blocklist also does not cover non-private ranges such as CGNAT 100.64.0.0/10, which ipaddress does not mark as private, loopback, link-local or reserved. Redirects are disabled, which limits the impact. Severity MEDIUM. It is a bypassable guard and is not trivially exploitable.

socket.getaddrinfo(parsed.hostname, ...) is the first DNS resolution, used only for validation
Blocklist check: is_private, is_loopback, is_link_local and is_reserved. The resolved address is discarded and is not pinned for the request.
requests.get(url, ...) performs a second, separate DNS resolution on the original hostname and fetches it. The response body (first 200 chars) is returned.

finding.guards_checked: The scheme check and the resolve-then-blocklist IP check were evaluated. The skill treats only strict hostname set membership, or an equivalent network-layer CIDR egress control, as closing a finding. Neither is present. The resolved IP is not pinned to the connection, which leaves the rebinding window open. allow_redirects=False is set and there is no manual Location re-fetch, so the redirect-based bypass does not apply here. I found no in-repo egress firewall config and no authentication on the route.
